title: Man shot by officer identified; Family grieves for 42-year-old killed during robbery at Parkdale pharmacy
article: The man shot dead by a Toronto police officer last Saturdayhas been identified.
David Fetterly, 42, was struck by a single bullet in the chest at a Roncesvalles pharmacy around 3 50 a.m.
The Special Investigations Unit, a civilian agency that probes cases of serious injury or death involving police, held off announcing Fetterly's name at the request of the family until yesterday.
"That name was never supposed to be released. We don't want to talk. This has been very hard. It's been a very difficult year," said a family member reached at his Toronto home.
What he was alluding to is another recent family tragedy.
On July 3, Fetterly's 16-year-old niece Chantele was stabbed in the heart outside her Hamilton home. She died in her mother's arms.
Since then, Sandra Fetterly-Brown has been leading an online crusade to have the teenager charged in her daughter's death tried as an adult.
Fetterly-Brown was one of a few dozen family members who have posted on an online tribute page for Fetterly.
"I can't take no more deaths in our family. It's tearing me up inside and I'm so confused," Fetterly-Brown wrote.
"I'm lost David without you! You were my only brother and my best friend.
"Although we all went our separate ways when we got older I know I could call on you for anything and you the same."
An SIU spokesperson said the investigation was continuing.

Officials have assigned seven investigators to the case and there is one subject officer. An area canvass was completed earlier in the week and as a result several civilian witnesses have been identified, said acting spokesperson Kaia Werbus.

Part of the reason the SIU withheld Fetterly's name for the past week is because officials wanted to give the family some time to speak about some "confidential information" regarding the investigation, Werbus said.

Toronto police have said the night Fetterly was shot, an on-duty officer was walking by Solarski Pharmacy, at Roncesvalles Ave. and Garden Ave., when he heard the store's security alarm. Fetterly had apparently broken in and was ransacking the pharmacy.
Police said there was a "physical altercation" before the officer fired his weapon.
Many of the comments online questioned why the officer shot to kill.
"The police officer should never had entered the store without backup ... my brother would not fight back, where is the store video?"Fetterly-Brown wrote.
